args.summary:
Session wrap-up (turns 83 to 88). The Pontic tribes besieged Jerusalem and we lost it. Then, on turn 87, they forced a peace on me ("the war is lost") while my 20k army was marching to take the city back, so my counterattack was cancelled with no warning. That feels abrupt. I'd expect a peace offer, or at least a heads-up that war weariness was about to end the war.

Main problems:
1) On the siege defence card, the Withdraw/Auto/Command buttons and the confirm button are hidden under the 'Army idle' toast and the banner. I only reached them by scrolling the card.
2) In the siege battle my army went from 52% to 0% a few seconds after I tapped Rally. No message explained it.
3) After that I could only sit through a long wait on an empty field, even on 3x speed.

What worked: the battle report is clear, the march preview shows turns and supply, and the turn report with its autosave note is tidy. We also met the Ahhiyawa this turn. Overall the war loop is interesting, but losing a city and

thought: Peace was forced on me just as my counterattack was on the way. Abrupt, but this is the last step, so I'm wrapping up.

args.summary: I played on from turn 116 to turn 123 as Israel, at war with Akkad. I founded Gezer, spent ruler points and let the advisor fill a production queue. The siege on Sippar seems to have stopped without any clear message saying why. I fought one RTS defence on Command. My only warband went to 0 just after I used Rally Cry, and nothing on screen said whether it died, routed or whether Rally Cry worked. The enemy hut I had burned to 1% then read 82%. I won only because the clock ran out with 3 buildings left. That is a hollow win and the battle feedback needs work. Autosave, 3x speed and end turn all worked smoothly. Gold is growing well (672, +93). Turn pacing feels good overall.

args.summary: Late information-age session. The core loop works and is stable: advisor builds, end turn, event cards, a peace deal. The peace screen stands out because it says exactly why the AI refuses each demand, and white peace with Pontus went through cleanly. Problems: the late game turns into a chore. Almost every turn means tapping Advisor builds, then End Turn, with no real choices. Several event cards only offer gold vs slightly more gold, which is not a real decision. With 33k gold and +1900 per turn the economy has no pressure left. The Kerma war moves without me, and nothing points me back to it. Ideas: a per-city auto-production toggle so cities stop asking each turn, event cards with real trade-offs, and something late game to spend gold on.

Late-game turns move quickly, but they are mostly tapping through prompts, so fun is moderate.
